author: Zach Mathis
description:
The main DFIR purpose is to capture files that attackers copy over via RDP, attacker commands that were copied and pasted, etc...
This event is generated when the system clipboard contents change.
Passwords and other sensitive information may be leaked when copied into the clipboard so heavy filtering to prevent this is necessary.
The copied contents are not saved in the event log but archived to the same protected folder as the File Delete event does. (C:\Sysmon)
SYSTEM privileges are required to access this folder. 
Hashes of the files can also be saved.
Session is where the process writing to clipboard is running: System(0), Interactive, Remote, etc...
ClientInfo will store originating hostname and IP address in the case of a remote session. (i.e. Attacker using RDP.)

author: Zach Mathis
description:
(From ultimatewindowsecurity.com)
This log is generated when
1. A user connects to a server or runs a program locally using alternate credentials.
   For instance a user maps a drive to a server but specifies a different user's credentials or opens a shortcut under RunAs by shift-control-right-clicking on the shortcut,
   selecting Run as..., and then filling in a different user's credentials in the dialog box that appears.  Or a user logs on to a web site using new specific credentials.
2. When a process logs on as a different account such as when the Scheduled Tasks service starts a task as the specified user.
3. With User Account Control enabled, an end user runs a program requiring admin authority.  You will get this event where the process information is consent.exe.
   Unfortunately the Subject does not identify the end user.
4. Logging on interactively to a server with a domain account. (Two 4624 events will also be generated.)
This logon event is unique in that it is logged on the source computer and not the target computer like most other logon events.
Also, it will be logged regardless of the logon being successful or not so consider it an attempt and not necessarily an actual successful logon.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Security' AND EventID=4648) AND (NOT COALESCE(((TargetUserName LIKE '%$' ESCAPE '\' OR SubjectUserName LIKE '%$' ESCAPE '\') OR (TargetUserName REGEXP '(DWM|UMFD)-([0-9]|1[0-3])$' AND IpAddress='-') OR (ProcessName LIKE '%powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE '%WMIC.exe' ESCAPE '\')), 0))
title: Explicit Logon Attempt

author: Zach Mathis
description:
Logon for RDS (Remote Desktop Services). Formerly known as Terminal Services.
Uses RDP so I am refering to these as RDP Logons as that is what most people will expect.
On newer OSes (Win 7+, 2012+), this event is logged only when a user successfully logs on to a RDP session.
On older OSes (Vista, 2008), this event is logged when a user logs on to a RDP session, regardless of success.

User and domain names are empty if the server is configured with Restricted Admin.
Information in this event is also found in the Security event log.

author: Zach Mathis
description:
The process accessed event reports when a process opens another process, an operation that is often followed by information queries or reading and writing the address space of the target process.

Enabling it can generate significant amounts of logging if there are diagnostic utilities active that repeatedly open processes to query their state, so it generally should only be done so with filters that remove expected accesses.
Source User and Target User are not available in earlier versions of Sysmon.

author: Zach Mathis
description:
Blue Screen Of Death. MS calls these Bug Check Errors.
param1 will contain various error codes for debugging:
example: 0x0000009f (0x0000000000000003, 0xffffe682fdfaf570, 0xfffff800666c4750, 0xffffe6831844f050)
    - 0x0000009f is the Bug Check Code (a.k.a. Stop Code) meaning DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE
    - 0x0000000000000003 indicates the type of inconsistency. In this case, 0x3 means the system is transitioning from a sleep state (S4 or S5) to an awake state (S0).
    - 0xffffe682fdfaf570 is a pointer to the DEVICE_OBJECT structure representing the device that is being enumerated.
    - 0xfffff800666c4750 is a pointer to the IRP (I/O Request Packet) that was pending for the device object.
    - 0xffffe6831844f050 is a pointer to the NTSTATUS code indicating the cause of the failure.
param2 is the path to a memory dump (ex: C:\WINDOWS\MEMORY.DMP)
param3 is the report ID (ex: cf65ecb3-8a81-4a04-89ae-8d1fff1aecf8)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='System' AND ProviderName='Microsoft-Windows-WER-SystemErrorReporting' AND EventID=1001
title: BSOD

author: Zach Mathis
description:
The CreateRemoteThread (Process Injection) event detects when a process creates a thread in another process. 
This technique is used by malware to inject code and hide in other processes. 
The event indicates the source and target process. 
It gives information on the code that will be run in the new thread: StartAddress, StartModule and StartFunction. 
Note that StartModule and StartFunction fields are inferred, they might be empty if the starting address is outside loaded modules or known exported functions.

title: Proc Injection

author: Zach Mathis
description:
The main DFIR purpose is to capture files that attackers copy over via RDP, attacker commands that were copied and pasted, etc...
This event is generated when the system clipboard contents change.
Passwords and other sensitive information may be leaked when copied into the clipboard so heavy filtering to prevent this is necessary.
The copied contents are not saved in the event log but archived to the same protected folder as the File Delete event does. (C:\Sysmon)
SYSTEM privileges are required to access this folder. 
Hashes of the files can also be saved.
Session is where the process writing to clipboard is running: System(0), Interactive, Remote, etc...
ClientInfo will store originating hostname and IP address in the case of a remote session. (i.e. Attacker using RDP.)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=24) AND (NOT COALESCE((RuleName='' OR RuleName='-'), 0))
title: Clipboard Change (Sysmon Alert)

The telemetry for this event was added for Windows 8.1 so it is not available on Windows 7 and earlier.

title: DNS Query (Sysmon Alert)

author: rukawa
description: Detects a suspicious RDP session redirect using tscon.exe
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND EventID=4688 AND CommandLine LIKE '%/dest%rdp-tcp%' ESCAPE '\'
title: Possible RDP Hijacking

author: Zach Mathis
description: On Powershell v5+, Windows will automatically log suspicious powershell execution and mark the Level as Warning.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND EventID=4104 AND Level=3
title: Potentially Malicious PwSh

author: Zach Mathis, Eric Conrad
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND EventID=4688 AND NewProcessName LIKE '%cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%.\\pipe%' ESCAPE '\'
title: Susp CmdLine (Possible Meterpreter getsystem)

author: Eric Conrad, Zach Mathis
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='System' AND EventID=7045 AND ImagePath REGEXP '^%SYSTEMROOT%\\[a-zA-Z]{8}\.exe$'
title: Possible Metasploit Svc Installed

author: Zach Mathis
description:
This Registry event type identifies Registry value modifications.
The event records the value written for Registry values of type DWORD and QWORD.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=13) AND (NOT COALESCE((RuleName='' OR RuleName='-'), 0))
title: Reg Key Value Set (Sysmon Alert)

author: Zach Mathis
description: Logs when a file gets deleted.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=26) AND (NOT COALESCE((RuleName='' OR RuleName='-'), 0))
title: File Deleted (Sysmon Alert)

author: Zach Mathis
description: The system has booted up. It also contains information about the OS version even though this information is not present in the event message. You can tell if the system was started up normally or in safe mode depending on the value of the BootMode. 0 for normal boot. 1 for Safe Mode. 2 for Safe Mode with networking.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='System' AND Provider_Name='Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-General' AND EventID=12) AND (NOT COALESCE((BootMode=0), 0))
title: Computer Startup In Safe Mode

author: Zach Mathis
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=6 AND Signed='true') AND (NOT COALESCE((ImageLoaded LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImageLoaded LIKE 'C:\\Program Files%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImageLoaded LIKE 'C:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))
title: Driver Loaded (Suspicious Path)

author: Zach Mathis
description: Tries to detect token impersonation by tools like Cobalt Strike.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Security' AND EventID=4624 AND LogonType=9) AND (NOT COALESCE((ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\svchost.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0))
title: NewInteractive Logon (Suspicious Process)

author: Zach Mathis
description:
A file was deleted. Additionally to logging the event, the deleted file is also saved in the ArchiveDirectory (which is C:\Sysmon by default). 
Under normal operating conditions this directory might grow to an unreasonable size - see event ID 26: FileDeleteDetected for similar behavior but without saving the deleted files.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=23) AND (NOT COALESCE((RuleName='' OR RuleName='-'), 0))
title: Deleted File Archived (Sysmon Alert)

author: Eric Conrad, Zach Mathis
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='System' AND EventID=7040 AND param1='Windows Event Log' AND param3='disabled'
title: Event Log Service Startup Type Changed To Disabled

author: Zach Mathis
description: Detects when powershell or cmd is used in WMI. (For persistence, lateral movement, etc...)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-WMI-Activity/Operational' AND EventID=5861) AND UserDataPossibleCause LIKE '%CommandLineEventConsumer%' ESCAPE '\' AND (UserDataPossibleCause LIKE '%powershell%' ESCAPE '\' OR UserDataPossibleCause LIKE '%cmd%' ESCAPE '\')
title: WMI Filter To Consumer Binding_Command Execution

author: Zach Mathis
description:
The RawAccessRead event detects when a process conducts reading operations from the drive using the \\.\ denotation. 
This technique is often used by malware for data exfiltration of files that are locked for reading, as well as to avoid file access auditing tools. 
The event indicates the source process and target device.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=9
title: Raw Access Read

author: Zach Mathis
description: This event logs when a named pipe connection is made between a client and a server.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=18) AND (NOT COALESCE((RuleName='' OR RuleName='-'), 0))
title: Pipe Connected (Sysmon Alert)

author: Yusuke Matsui, Zach Mathis
description: An attacker may have started Powershell 2.0 to evade detection.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Windows PowerShell' AND EventID=400 AND Data LIKE '%EngineVersion=2%' ESCAPE '\'
title: PwSh 2.0 Downgrade Attack

author: Zach Mathis
description:
Detects process hollowing or process herpaderping techniques which would normally not be visible in Task Manager.
Process hollowing is when malware launches a legitimate process in a suspended state and replaces legitimate code in the process with malicious code. 
This malicious code is then executed by the process, with whatever permissions are assigned to the process.
Process herpaderping is where malware modifies its image on the disk to look like legitimate software after the malware is loaded. 
When security software scans the on-disk file, it will see a harmless file while the malicious code runs in memory.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=25
title: Proc Tampering

author: Zach Mathis
description:
File create operations are logged when a file is created or overwritten. 
This event is useful for monitoring autostart locations, like the Startup folder, as well as temporary and download directories, which are common places malware drops during initial infection.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=11) AND (NOT COALESCE((RuleName='' OR RuleName='-'), 0))
title: File Created (Sysmon Alert)

author: Zach Mathis
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=6 AND SignatureStatus='Expired') AND (NOT COALESCE((Signed='true'), 0))
title: Driver Loaded (Expired/Revoked Cert)

author: Yusuke Matsui, Zach Mathis
description: For each account found without preauthentication, an adversary may send an AS-REQ message without the encrypted timestamp and receive an AS-REP message with TGT data which may be encrypted with an insecure algorithm such as RC4.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND EventID=4768 AND TicketEncryptionType='0x17' AND PreAuthType='0'
title: Possible AS-REP Roasting (RC4 Kerberos Ticket Req)

author: Zach Mathis
description: Display network connection with sysmon rule alerts. Disabled by default.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=3) AND (NOT COALESCE((RuleName='' OR RuleName='-'), 0))
title: Net Conn (Sysmon Alert)

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Zach Mathis
description: Somebody cleared an imporant event log.
falsepositives: Rollout of log collection agents (the setup routine often includes a reset of the local Eventlog)
System provisioning (system reset before the golden image creation)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='System' AND Provider_Name='Microsoft-Windows-Eventlog' AND EventID=104) AND (NOT COALESCE((LogFileClearedChannel='Application' OR LogFileClearedChannel='Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational' OR LogFileClearedChannel='Microsoft-Windows-AppLocker/EXE and DLL' OR LogFileClearedChannel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR LogFileClearedChannel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' OR LogFileClearedChannel='Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational' OR LogFileClearedChannel='OpenSSH/Operational' OR LogFileClearedChannel='Security' OR LogFileClearedChannel='System' OR LogFileClearedChannel='Windows PowerShell'), 0))
title: Log File Cleared

author: Zach Mathis
description: Registry key and value create and delete operations map to this event type, which can be useful for monitoring for changes to Registry autostart locations, or specific malware registry modifications.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=12) AND (NOT COALESCE((RuleName='' OR RuleName='-'), 0))
title: Reg Key Create/Delete (Sysmon Alert)

author: Yusuke Matsui, Zach Mathis
description: Adversaries may abuse a valid Kerberos ticket-granting ticket (TGT) or sniff network traffic to obtain a ticket-granting service (TGS) ticket that may be vulnerable to Brute Force.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND EventID=4769 AND TicketEncryptionType='0x17'
title: Possible Kerberoasting (RC4 Kerberos Ticket Req)

author: Zach Mathis
description:
When a WMI event filter is registered, which is a method used by malware to execute, this event logs the WMI namespace, 
filter name and filter expression.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=20) AND (NOT COALESCE((RuleName='' OR RuleName='-'), 0))
title: WMI Event Consumer (Sysmon Alert)

author: Zach Mathis
description: PSExec is a MS SysInternals tool often abused for lateral movement.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='System' AND EventID=7045) AND (Service='PSEXESVC' OR ImagePath LIKE '%PSEXESVC%' ESCAPE '\')
title: PSExec Lateral Movement

author: Zach Mathis, Fukusuke Takahashi
description: Windows defender malware detection
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational' AND EventID=1116 AND SeverityID=4
title: Defender Alert (High)

author: Zach Mathis
description: Loaded driver was signed with an invalid signature.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=6 AND Signed='true') AND (NOT COALESCE((SignatureStatus='Valid'), 0))
title: Driver Loaded (Invalid Signature)

author: Zach Mathis
description:
The CreateRemoteThread (Process Injection) event detects when a process creates a thread in another process. 
This technique is used by malware to inject code and hide in other processes. 
The event indicates the source and target process. 
It gives information on the code that will be run in the new thread: StartAddress, StartModule and StartFunction. 
Note that StartModule and StartFunction fields are inferred, they might be empty if the starting address is outside loaded modules or known exported functions.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=8) AND (NOT COALESCE((RuleName='' OR RuleName='-'), 0))
title: Proc Injection (Sysmon Alert)

author: Zach Mathis
description: A user was added to the Domain Admins group. Only logged on DCs.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Security' AND EventID=4728 AND TargetUserName='Domain Admins') AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE '%$' ESCAPE '\'), 0))
title: User Added To Global Domain Admins Grp

author: Zach Mathis
description:
The process accessed event reports when a process opens another process, an operation that is often followed by information queries or reading and writing the address space of the target process. 
This enables detection of hacking tools that read the memory contents of processes like Local Security Authority (Lsass.exe) in order to steal credentials for use in Pass-the-Hash attacks. 
Enabling it can generate significant amounts of logging if there are diagnostic utilities active that repeatedly open processes to query their state, so it generally should only be done so with filters that remove expected accesses.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=10) AND (NOT COALESCE((RuleName='' OR RuleName='-'), 0))
title: Proc Access (Sysmon Alert)

author: Zach Mathis
description: A user was added to the local Administrators group. Unfortunately the user name does not get recorded in the log, only the SID, so you need to look up the username via the SID.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND EventID=4732 AND TargetUserName='Administrators'
title: User Added To Local Admin Grp

author: Zach Mathis
description: A computer account (an account that ends with a $) was created. These accounts are not displayed by default so will be hidden.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND EventID=4720 AND TargetUserName LIKE '%$' ESCAPE '\'
title: Hidden User Account Created

author: Zach Mathis
description: Detects explicit credential logons with suspicous processes like powershell and wmic which are often abused by malware like Cobalt Strike or Mimikatz for user impersonation.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Security' AND EventID=4648) AND (ProcessName LIKE '%powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE '%WMIC.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE(((TargetUserName LIKE '%$' ESCAPE '\' AND IpAddress='-') AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE '%$' ESCAPE '\'), 0))), 0)) AND (NOT COALESCE((TargetUserName REGEXP '(DWM|UMFD)-([0-9]|1[0-3])$' AND IpAddress='-'), 0)) AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE '%$' ESCAPE '\' AND TargetUserName LIKE '%$' ESCAPE '\' AND TargetInfo LIKE '%$' ESCAPE '\'), 0))
title: Explicit Logon Attempt (Susp Proc) - Possible Mimikatz PrivEsc

author: Zach Mathis
description: Sysmon blocked file shredding from a tool like SDelete.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=28
title: File Shredding Tool Blocked

author: Zach Mathis
description: Checks whether the image specified in a process creation event doesn't refer to an .exe file.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=1) AND (NOT COALESCE((Image LIKE '%.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR (Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\scrnsave.scr' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\scrnsave.scr' ESCAPE '\')), 0))

description: Sysmon blocked an .exe file from being written to disk based on various suspicious conditions.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND EventID=27
title: Blocked Exe File Creation

author: Zach Mathis
description: A user was added to the local Domain Admins group.

title: User Added To Local Domain Admins Grp

title: Log Cleared

description: Sysmon process creation

description: Malware will often create services for persistence and use BASE64 encoded strings to execute malicious code or abuse legitimate binaries like cmd.exe, powershell, etc... inside the path to execute. Normally, services will not run built-in binaries, run from user or temp folders or contain encoded data.
